The spec schema: the arguments a spec item may give, and their types

Source: R/schema.R
tfl_schema.Rd

A spec's content: lists items, one a function call (tfl_item()): the function, its arguments by name. The schema says what each takes – the type of a value where the spec writes it differently from R (a YAML map for a named vector, a list of rows for a data frame, !r for an expression), and the grammar of ... for the functions whose body is ... (plan_cells(), plan_digits(), plan_sort() and ten more). The same file is what the GUI's help and the AI kit's schema read.

Usage

tfl_schema(fn = NULL)

Arguments

fn

A function's name ("plan_cells"), or NULL for all.

Value

The function's entry (package, description, dots, args; rank, its place in the recommended order, and stage, "mapping", "finishing" or "output"; formals, the function's own arguments but the data's (x, plan, .plan, data, mapping), and required, those of them with no default value), or the whole schema, a list by function; NULL for a function the schema does not have.

Details

A figure's functions: the file has a card for those a clinical figure uses (the geoms and the stats – those with no geom of their own and those with one –, scales and the limits xlim(), ylim(), lims(), expand_limits(), coordinates, complete themes, theme() and its parts theme_sub_*(), elements, guides, positions, annotation_*(), a facet's vars() and labellers); any other function of a plot ggplot2 exports (coord_quickmap, geom_sf_text) is its formals. ggplot2's other spellings (scale_color_manual, guide_colorbar, theme_grey, stat_bin2d) read as the card of the function they spell, and the code keeps the name written. So are the extension packages' (ggsurvfit's add_risktable() and themes, ggrepel, ggh4x's facets and strips, ggtext's elements, ggnewscale, patchwork's arrangement): those a clinical figure uses have a card, any other of a plot is named pkg::fn (ggh4x::facet_manual). The arguments the functions of one kind share – a layer's stat, position, fun.data, pad; a scale's name, breaks, labels, sec.axis; theme()'s settings, each its element – are typed and labelled by inst/fig/gg_args.csv for every function that takes them. A geom given another stat (geom_step(stat = "ecdf")) is checked with that stat's parameters too, a stat given another geom with that geom's. A layer takes what any layer passes on to layer() (key_glyph, ggplot2 4.0's layout) and its position's (ggplot2 4.0's nudge_x / nudge_y of geom_text()); an argument by ggplot2's other spelling of an aesthetic (color, pch, lty) is checked as the one it spells. theme() takes ggplot2 4.0's default palettes (palette.colour.discrete ...).

The types, in a short notation: string, integer, number (a number written as arithmetic of numbers, !r 1/5, is one), logical, enum[a|b], column, stat, template, r (!r), formula (!r, written ~ <text>), guard (!r, a two-sided cond ~ "text"), function (a function by its name, mean_se or Hmisc::smean.cl.normal, written bare: fun.data = mean_se), tilde (a formula as its text, y ~ x or ~ . / 7, written as the formula), date (a date as its text, 2024-01-01; a sequence of them, NA an open end, written as.Date(c("2024-01-01", NA))), call and call<fn> ({fn:, args:}; call<label_*> takes any function whose name the pattern matches, of any package: {fn: scales::label_percent}; base R's that clinical figures write as a value are typed where they fit: seq() for breaks, {fn: seq, args: {from: 0, to: 52, by: 4}} written seq(0, 52, by = 4); alpha() for a colour; grDevices' palettes, hcl.colors() ..., for a scale's colours), list<T> (a sequence), vec<K, V> (a map that is a named vector in R), map<K, V> (a map that is a named list), rows<f1, f2, ...> (a sequence of maps that is a data frame) and T|U (either).

An argument's entry also says how a form shows it: label, its short English name (a GUI translates it and writes "label (argument)"), help, a sentence or two a form's "?" shows (the description is what the AI kit and the reference read), and main: true for the arguments a form shows from the start (the others folded under the function's other arguments). colour is a colour's text (#RRGGBB).

A layer's entry (geom_errorbar) says its aesthetics too: aes, the names a mapping takes (an unknown one warns, as ggplot2 does; color is colour), aes_required, those it needs, and aes_or, a required one's alternatives (ymin or xmin: a bar across). A figure's plot is checked for them: a layer missing a required aesthetic, neither mapped nor given a value nor inherited from ggplot()'s mapping, warns.

A mapping's value is a column's name (colour: TRTA), or an expression of a mapping's form, written as its text, untagged: a call of factor(), as.factor(), ordered(), as.numeric(), as.integer(), as.character(), interaction(), reorder(), rev(), abs(), sqrt(), exp(), log() / log2() / log10() / log1p(), round(), after_stat(), after_scale(), stage(), ifelse(), cut(), is.na(), nchar(), toupper() / tolower(), substr() or trimws(), or of the arithmetic or a comparison (<, <=, ==, !=, %in%, !, &, |), of columns, constants, their arithmetic and c(), sum(), max(), min(), mean(), median(), length(), alpha(), pmin(), pmax(), cumsum(), [, duplicated(), unique(), rank() (x: factor(AVISITN), y: after_stat(density), x: reorder(USUBJID, -PCHG), fill: after_scale(alpha(colour, 0.4)), a waterfall's fill: PCHG <= -30 or fill: ifelse(PCHG <= -30, "PR", "SD/PD"); in YAML a text that starts with ! is quoted, '!is.na(ADT)'); a number is a constant (group: 1). A column whose name R does not write bare is written in backticks (x: `A-B`, as code is read back); written tight (A-B) it is read as the expression, and the check warns. Any other R is !r. The check warns for a text of neither form (it is written as a column of that name) and for a variable of after_stat() the layer's stat does not compute (after_stat(densty)).

See also

tfl_schema_check()
